Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Shri Rama Niwas Pathak, learned counsel for respondent no.2 as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

2. In terms of the F.I.R., it was alleged that the informant was a resident of Ayodhya and on 31.7.2023 at about 12.20 p.m., when she was going to bring her children from the school, she met with he applicant who was the friend of her husband and the applicant offered her to take her in his auto to be dropped at the school.

Believing him, she sat on his auto and therafter he stopped on the way to his sister home and asked her to come in the home as his sister wanted to meet her and thereafter he committed offence of rape against her.

1 3.
In the statements under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., the victim disclosed her age as 27 years.
In her statement, she stated that the offence was committed on 2.8.2023 and not on 31.8.2023.
On being confronted, she specifically stated that as her mental condition was not proper, as such in the F.I.R., she mentioned the date as 31.7.2023 whereas the incident occurred on 2.8.2023.
A similar statement was given under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
The F.I.R. in question was lodged on 13.8.2023 allegedly after about 11 days of the incident.
The medical on record naturally does not support the allegation levelled in the F.I.R.

The applicant is in custody since 17.8.2023 and has no criminal history, hence the applicant may be enlarged on bail.
4.
Learned A.G.A. also opposed the prayer for bail.

5. Considering the fact that the victim is married lady and there is prima facie no explanation for the inordinate delay in lodging the F.I.R. apart from the statement of the victim under Section 161 Cr.P.C. which itself contains contradictions and the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., and there is no material on record to corroborate the allegations of the F.I.R as such the applicant who has no criminal antecedents and is in custody since 17.8.2023 and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
6.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Satya Prakash @ Satyapal Jaiswal @ Bachha be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.513 of 2023, under Sections 376 and 506 I.P.C., Police Station Kotwali Nagar, District Faizabad/Ayodhya on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions :-
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
